Referral Note

43-year-old elementary school teacher referred for psychiatric evaluation of depression that has worsened over the past seven weeks. She reports persistent sadness nearly every day, loss of interest in activities she previously enjoyed, fatigue, insomnia, decreased appetite, excessive guilt, feelings of worthlessness, and difficulty concentrating. She is struggling to complete lesson plans and has begun calling in sick because she lacks the energy to work, and she has withdrawn from family activities despite a supportive husband. She disclosed passive thoughts that “my family would probably be better off without me” and denies a plan or intent. She denies any history of elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, impulsivity, excessive spending, increased goal-directed activity, hallucinations, or delusions. No prior psychiatric treatment. Mother has recurrent major depressive disorder. Workup in this office, including CBC, CMP, thyroid studies, vitamin B12, and vitamin D, is unremarkable. Referred for diagnostic evaluation and treatment recommendations.

Behavioral Observations (on arrival)

Appearance: Appropriately dressed. Appears fatigued; tearful throughout the interview.

Behavior: Cooperative and engaged, though slowed. Alert and fully oriented.

Speech: Slow but coherent.

Mood / Affect: Describes mood as “hopeless”; affect constricted and congruent with mood.

Thought / Perception: Thought processes logical and goal directed. Endorses passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent. Denies homicidal ideation. No hallucinations or delusions.

Cognition / Insight: Alert and fully oriented. Insight fair; judgment intact.
